design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (flood_coverage_and_mortgagee_billing).
[Draw] draw_counts.py --task 1: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 6, 5]; the increase charge took 6 factors, the credit 5, the refund 4.
[Why a good test] Cornelius asks only for the unused premium back. The refund rule waits on the cancellation credit (state form); the credit rule waits on an additional-premium charge for every recorded limit increase (state form); the records show a pending unsigned request and an unbilled July increase. The agent must charge the increase (6 rules; the endorsement's request-time figure 110.94 is exactly the baseline and wrong), have the insured sign the cancellation with the credit (5 rules incl. the returned increase charge and the loss-avoidance deduction), then refund (4 rules incl. the HomeGuard offset). Breadth: 15 billing rows, 6 claim rows, endorsement, request, HomeGuard (cross-product).
[Scope] Occupied by task 0: flood_ext_renewal_indication/term/payment and tools record_flood_renewal_offer_81f1ff73, renew_flood_policy_8cc307a9, pay_flood_renewal_premium_ad8d78a5. This task claims flood_ext_increase_premium, flood_ext_cancellation_credit, flood_ext_cancellation_refund and bill_flood_increase_premium_f099355d, sign_flood_cancellation_83daa4cf (owner=user), issue_flood_refund_b526defb. Nothing is left unclaimed.
[Problem-tree card] root flood_ext_cancellation_refund. Edge refund -> credit: value_input, gate credits_posted, form state, sentence 'No refund is paid out until the premium account carries the cancellation credit for the policy's signed cancellation.' (negated; only the signing write posts a cancellation credit). False at opening: request 5d5c550b-63c0-4687-8554-880ca747794c pending_signature, no flood_return_premium entry. Edge credit -> increase: value_input, gate addl_billed, form state, sentence 'The cancellation credit is worked out only after the premium account carries an additional-premium charge for every limit increase recorded on the policy with additional premium due.' (affirmative; only the increase-charge write posts an additional premium). False at opening: endorsement 49d8dd0b-5407-438c-976d-e4ea590ed45a premium_direction additional with no charge. Four-point test holds for both (ordering connective, record-visible state, no code token, exact scope 'every limit increase recorded on the policy with additional premium due', matching the condition premium_direction additional). Deletion sensitivity (run): skip the increase charge -> credit 203.37 instead of 294.33; skip the signing -> refund recompute raises (no cancellation date) and the account is in debit. Owner=user problem: the cancellation must be signed by the named insured (flood_cancellation 'on a request the named insured has signed'); it completes on the spot.
[Base-invariant card] increase charge (flood_additional_premium): flood_billing_and_mortgagee, policy_scope. cancellation (flood_policy_cancelled, flood_return_premium): flood_cancellation.accepted_reason — request 5d5c550b-63c0-4687-8554-880ca747794c states property_sold (accepted, pro_rata), correlated by flood_request_id; backdating 11 days <= 30 and not before the 2026-04-11 effective date. refund (flood_refund_issued): flood_billing_and_mortgagee, policy_scope; payer = payer of the latest payment (insured).
[Business-object card] Object: FG-5361-0927 (01b5566c-16d6-4a1f-93de-3014d40200db); the increase charge carries source_endorsement_id 49d8dd0b-5407-438c-976d-e4ea590ed45a; the credit is tied to request 5d5c550b-63c0-4687-8554-880ca747794c; the refund balances this policy's ledger only; the HomeGuard balance 46.18 is read, never written (the offset reduces the flood refund only).
[Factor card] increase: earned-share method whole months 8/12 (baseline 251/365 -> 95.74); increase companion 10% (cross home, multi-source; baseline -> 103.13); layer share 0.85 (-> 109.19); anti-selection 25% (-> 74.25); insurance-to-value 5% (-> 97.70); mitigation 5% (multi-source; near-miss the 2024 reimbursement 26 months back; -> 97.70). Whole baseline 110.94 (= the stale endorsement quote). credit: unearned day count (method, cross home, multi-source) 213/365 (-> 291.58); increase premium return (method) full 92.81 (-> 203.37); claim deduction 418.60 (-> 712.93; near-miss 2024 reimbursement outside 12 months); fee return 0.5 (-> 256.83); backdating 2% (-> 308.11). Whole baseline 593.60. refund: offset order (method, cross home, multi-source) 46.18 (-> 196.51); interest rate 3% (-> 151.46); interest anchor 2 days (method, cross home; -> 151.63); card charge 2.5% (-> 155.37). Whole baseline 201.52.
[Overwrites] increase supersedes the base limit-increase proration sentence; credit supersedes the pro_rata/flat/fee sentence and the claim-paid fully-earned sentence of flood_cancellation; refund supersedes the base refund sentence of flood_billing_and_mortgagee. All other base clauses (accepted reasons, backdating max 30 days, minimum premium change, refund minimum) stay inherited.
[Seed] 15 billing rows across four terms (settled, one returned payment 2023 near-miss), endorsement, 6 claim rows (two loss-avoidance-only claims), pending request, HomeGuard ended at the sale with 46.18 owed. No other obligation is lit: claims closed, terms settled. The HomeGuard's 46.18 owed (its ledger: 2310.00 billed, 158.40 additional premium, 2310.00 paid, 112.22 short-rate return on the 2026-09-11 cancellation) is held back from the flood refund; it is not written by any step of this task, so after gold the flood account keeps the 46.18 held back (plus the 3.88 card charge less the 0.03 interest, a 50.03 credit) and the HomeGuard still shows 46.18 owed — re-applying the refund rule to the terminal world gives about 3.75, below the 5.00 refund minimum, so no further refund is due.
[Persona] Brisk retired engineer; volunteers the sale, the closing date and the goal; gives credentials, policy number, the web form, the HomeGuard and the July increase only when asked; signs when handed the step; accepts retentions; ends on 'refund issued'. Never states a figure.
[Reachability] All at frozen_time 2026-09-24 14:40; the sale and the web form happened before the call and are on record; the signing is done on the call.
[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> reads (policy, billing, endorsements, claims, request, HomeGuard, HomeGuard ledger, umbrella) -> charge increase 92.81 -> hand over signing (2026-09-11, pro_rata, 294.33) -> refund 151.49 to the insured by card.
[Verification] Values from the gate's own evaluator on each handling-time world: 92.81, 294.33, 151.49; check_compute --task 1 recomputes them.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] refund waits on a cancellation credit -> none; credit waits on increase charges -> the July increase is unbilled -> charge it (92.81) -> credit (294.33) -> refund (151.49). Same as gold.

[Revision round 2 — audit audits/policy_task/flood_coverage_and_mortgagee_billing] R-1-1: the charter no longer says 'the date the signed cancellation request was received'; the credit (backdating, unsigned-sale day count) and refund (interest anchor) rules now read 'the date the cancellation request was received, as recorded on the request whether or not it had been signed by then', so the only receipt date is created_at 2026-09-22 and the refund is uniquely 151.49 (the 151.46 reading no longer has a textual basis). R-1-2: the [Seed] card no longer claims the HomeGuard balance is consumed; the refund rule now says the amount is held back against the other balance and stays on the flood account, and the terminal residue is stated. O-1-2: the persona's reaction line no longer anticipates retention or the HomeGuard offset. O-1-4: four home_billing rows now explain the 46.18 owed, read by find_home_billing (new evaluation step 8; later steps shift by one). O-G3g/h, O-G6b/c applied in the charter (mitigation window anchored at the posting date; HomeGuard 'in force on the request date' checks bound date and status; credit prerequisite scoped to increases with additional premium due; refund condition equals its sentence). Values unchanged: 92.81, 294.33, 151.49. Kept as observations: O-1-1 (the unposted increase charge is the posting backlog this task resolves; the seed shows the coverage update without its charge), O-1-3/O-G7 (the held-back amount is applied on the HomeGuard line, which no write of this difficulty touches).
[Revision round 3 — audit revision_2] N-1-1: the [Problem-tree card] and the increase-charge step's necessity now quote the current prerequisite sentence ('... for every limit increase recorded on the policy with additional premium due.'). N-G6 (charter): a HomeGuard still pending cancellation or nonrenewal counts as in force on the request date; inert here (the HomeGuard was in force on 2026-07-20 and closed 2026-09-11). Values unchanged: 92.81, 294.33, 151.49.
user_scenario: You are Cornelius Vandermolen-Achebe, a 68-year-old retired civil engineer: brisk, organised, short sentences, slightly impatient with small talk. You sold your house at 212 Mariemont Landing Road, Newtown, OH 45244 — the sale closed on 2026-09-11 — and you now live in Milford. You paid the flood insurance on that house for the whole year back in March, and since the house is no longer yours you are calling to get back the money for the part of the year you will not be using. That is what you want done on this call, and you are happy for the agent to handle it. You give details only when asked: your phone number is 740-627-4183 and your date of birth is 1957-11-02; if more is needed, your mailing ZIP code is now 45150 and your email is c.vandermolen.achebe@olentangyridge.net. The flood policy number is FG-5361-0927 if they ask for it. If the agent asks whether you sent anything in, you say you filled in a form on the Larkspur website on the evening of the 22nd saying the house was sold. If asked about other policies, you say the homeowners policy on the same house ended at the closing and you think a small amount is still showing on it, and that you have no other Larkspur policies. If asked about changes this year, you say you raised the building coverage in July after the river scare in May, when Larkspur paid you back for the sandbags; you do not remember any figures. You do not know how any of the amounts are worked out and you never propose a number. If the agent explains that you have to sign something yourself, you agree, and when the agent hands the signing step over to you with the details to use, you complete it exactly as given and tell them what it shows. If the agent walks you through how the amount was worked out, you just say 'fine, as long as it is all settled' and let them carry on. When the agent tells you the refund has been issued, you thank them and hang up; you ask for nothing else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain: increase charge -> signed cancellation with credit -> refund. Each edge is a value dependency (the credit returns the increase charge; the refund pays the balance the credit creates), so no other order gives the same terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the signed cancellation leaves the policy in force with no closed_date and the account 92.81 in debit: the refund recompute has no cancellation date (raises) and no credit to pay, instead of 151.49; the policy/request rows also stay unchanged (terminal hash differs).
Skipping the increase charge gives a credit of 203.37 instead of 294.33 (nothing to return), and no additional-premium entry lands.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for the money for the unused part of the year; it never mentions a cancellation to sign, a cancellation credit, or the July increase charge. The web form and the July increase are mentioned only if the agent asks, and the signing happens only after the agent explains it and hands it over.
